Simulate multi-species data for a joint species distribution model

Source: R/sim_jsdgam.R
sim_jsdgam.Rd

Draws a site-by-species response matrix from a latent factor model and returns it in the long format jsdgam() takes. Each species gets its own intercept and its own slope on a site-level covariate. The species share n_lv latent factors, whose loadings set the residual correlation between them.

This is the non-detection counterpart to sim_closure_unit_data(), which simulates the same latent factor structure for the occupancy and N-mixture families.

Usage

sim_jsdgam(
  family = brms::negbinomial(),
  n_species = 5L,
  n_sites = 60L,
  n_lv = 2L,
  family_pars = list(),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

family

Observation family. Any family mvgam's response simulator draws from, plus mvn(), mvt(), diri(), multi() and categ(). Defaults to brms::negbinomial().

n_species

Number of species. Defaults to 5.

n_sites

Number of sites. Defaults to 60.

n_lv

Number of latent factors. Defaults to 2.

family_pars

Optional named list of family parameters: Psi (per-species scale for mvn() / mvt()), nu (degrees of freedom for mvt()), phi (concentration for diri()), unit_total (trial total per site for multi()). Other families take their dispersion or scale, such as size for a negative binomial or sigma for a gaussian.

seed

Optional integer seed. The session's random state is restored when the call returns.

Value

An object of class mvgam_sim_jsdgam, inheriting mvgam_sim, with elements:

data_train

Long data.frame with columns site, env, series (the species), y and time (the unit index jsdgam() keys on).

data_test

NULL, kept for consistency with the other simulators.

y_array

[n_sites x n_species] response matrix.

family

The family used.

n_species, n_sites, n_lv

The design.

truth

List of the generative parameters: loadings, lv, intercepts, env_slopes, env, residual_cov, residual_cor and family_pars. For mvn(), mvt(), diri() and multi() these include the defaults Psi = 0.5, nu = 5, phi = 30 and unit_total = 30.

Details

The linear predictor for species k at site i is intercept[k] + env_slope[k] * env[i] + Z[k, ] %*% lv[i, ], where Z holds the loadings and lv the site scores. The residual covariance the model targets is Z Z', plus a diagonal of squared per-species scales for mvn() and mvt().

How that predictor becomes a response depends on the family. Families whose species are drawn independently, such as brms::negbinomial() or stats::poisson(), take one draw per species. mvn() and mvt() add a per-species residual. The composition families draw a site's species together. diri() normalises gamma variates. multi() draws counts against a fixed site total. categ() draws one species per site as a one-hot row.

A composition family identifies its loadings only up to a shift shared by the species, which is the subspace mvgam's sum_to_zero_vector parameterisation covers. The loadings are centred for those families, which puts the simulated truth in the same subspace a fit explores.

How much of the factor structure survives into the response depends on the observation noise. The loadings are drawn with standard deviation 0.7. mvn() and mvt() take their per-species scale from Psi, which defaults to 0.5. Every other family takes the scale its own simulator defaults to. A gaussian's sigma defaults to 1, which can hide the species correlations from the data. Pass family_pars = list(sigma = 0.5) for a gaussian whose correlations a fit can recover.

See also

jsdgam() fits the model these data come from. sim_closure_unit_data() simulates occupancy and N-mixture data. sim_mvgam() simulates time series. The joint species distribution article fits and interprets models of this kind.

Other simulation: sim_closure_unit_data(), sim_mvgam()

Examples

simdat <- sim_jsdgam(
  family    = brms::negbinomial(),
  n_species = 4L,
  n_sites   = 30L,
  n_lv      = 2L,
  seed      = 1L
)
head(simdat$data_train)
#>   site        env series y time
#> 1    1  0.5757814   sp_1 4    1
#> 2    1  0.5757814   sp_2 1    1
#> 3    1  0.5757814   sp_3 0    1
#> 4    1  0.5757814   sp_4 1    1
#> 5    2 -0.3053884   sp_1 0    2
#> 6    2 -0.3053884   sp_2 2    2
summary(simdat)
#> Simulated joint species distribution dataset (sim_jsdgam)
#>   Family        : negbinomial
#>   Species       : 4
#>   Sites         : 30
#>   Latent factors: 2
#>   Rows          : 120
#> 
#> True generative parameters
#>   Intercepts :  1.100,  0.763, -0.165, -0.253
#>   Env slopes :  0.697,  0.557, -0.689, -0.707
#>   Residual correlations: [-0.680, 0.999]
#> 
#> Simulated response
#>   Range         : [ 0, 18]
#>   Zero fraction : 0.317

# A composition family draws each site's species together
comp <- sim_jsdgam(family = diri(), n_species = 4L, n_sites = 20L,
                   seed = 2L)
rowSums(comp$y_array)[1:3]
#> [1] 1 1 1

# Next: fit with jsdgam(), then compare residual_cor() of the fit
# with simdat$truth$residual_cor
